identificationModule.briefTitle: Quizartinib or Placebo Plus Chemotherapy in Newly Diagnosed Patients With FLT3-ITD Negative AML
identificationModule.officialTitle: A Phase 3, Double-Blind, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Trial Of Quizartinib Administered in Combination With Induction and Consolidation Chemotherapy and Administered as Maintenance Therapy in Adult Patients With Newly Diagnosed FLT3-ITD Negative Acute Myeloid Leukemia

descriptionModule.briefSummary: This study will compare the effects of Quizartinib versus placebo in combination with chemotherapy in participants with newly diagnosed FMS-like tyrosine kinase 3 (FLT3)-internal tandem duplication (ITD) negative acute myeloid leukemia (AML).
descriptionModule.detailedDescription: This is a clinical trial to compare the effect of quizartinib versus placebo (administered with standard induction and consolidation chemotherapy, then administered as maintenance therapy for up to 36 cycles) on the primary endpoint of overall survival (OS) in adult patients with newly diagnosed FMS-like tyrosine kinase 3 (FLT3)-internal tandem duplication (ITD) negative acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Participants will be tested for FLT3-ITD mutation status in a central laboratory using a validated assay.

maskingInfo.maskingDescription: This study has a double-blind design. Neither the participants nor any of the investigators, Sponsor, Independent Review Committee (IRC) or contract research organizations (CROs) will be aware of the treatments received. An independent biostatistician, not otherwise part of the Sponsor trial team, will generate the randomization schedule.

armGroups.label: Arm A: Quizartinib + Chemotherapy
armGroups.description: Participants will receive quizartinib at 60 mg/day orally once daily for 14 days starting after the completion of chemotherapy in Induction and Consolidation Phase. In the Maintenance Phase, participants will receive quizartinib at 60 mg/day orally once daily for up to 36 cycles (28-day cycle)

armGroups.label: Arm B: Placebo + Chemotherapy
armGroups.description: Participants will receive placebo at 60 mg/day orally once daily for 14 days starting after the completion of chemotherapy in Induction and Consolidation Phase. In the Maintenance Phase, participants will receive placebo at 60 mg/day orally once daily for up to 36 cycles (28-day cycle)

armGroups.label: Arm C: Quizartinib + Chemotherapy then Placebo Maintenance
armGroups.description: Participants will receive quizartinib at 60 mg/day orally once daily for 14 days starting after the completion of chemotherapy in Induction and Consolidation Phase. In the Maintenance Phase, participants will receive placebo at 60 mg/day orally once daily for up to 36 cycles (28-day cycle)

interventions.name: Quizartinib
interventions.description: Participants will receive quizartinib at 60 mg/day orally once daily
armGroupLabels: Arm C: Quizartinib + Chemotherapy then Placebo Maintenance

interventions.name: Placebo
interventions.description: Participants will receive placebo at 60 mg/day orally once daily
armGroupLabels: Arm C: Quizartinib + Chemotherapy then Placebo Maintenance

interventions.name: Chemotherapy
interventions.description: Participants will receive commercially available cytarabine (cytosine arabinoside) and anthracycline (daunorubicin or idarubicin).

primaryOutcomes.measure: Overall Survival (Arm A vs Arm B)
primaryOutcomes.description: Overall survival (OS) is defined as the time from randomization until death from any cause.
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Date of first patient randomized to the target number of deaths reached, up to approximately 42 months

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Event-free survival (Arm A vs. Arm B)
secondaryOutcomes.description: Event-free survival (EFS) is defined as time from randomization to date of failure to achieve CR at end of induction, relapse after CR, or death due to any cause, whichever occurs first
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Date of randomization up to approximately 42 months

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Duration of complete response (Arm A vs. Arm B)
secondaryOutcomes.description: Duration of complete response (DoCR) is defined as time from the first documented CR until documented relapse or death due to any cause, whichever comes first. As assessed by Independent Review Committee.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Date of randomization up to approximately 42 months

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Relapse-free survival (Arm A vs. Arm B)
secondaryOutcomes.description: Relapse-free survival (RFS) is defined as time from randomization, for participants who achieve CR in the Induction Phase, until relapse or death due to any cause, whichever comes first. As assessed by Independent Review Committee .
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Date of randomization up to approximately 42 months

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Complete remission rate (Arm A vs. Arm B)
secondaryOutcomes.description: Complete remission rate (CR) is defined as proportion of of participants who achieved a CR. As assessed by Independent Review Committee.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: At end of Induction Phase, up to approximately 120 days

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Complete remission rate with minimal or measurable residual disease (Arm A vs. Arm B)
secondaryOutcomes.description: Proportion of participants achieving CR with minimal or measurable residual disease (MRD) negativity. As assessed by Independent Review Committee.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: At end of Induction Phase (Cycle 2 or Cycles 1 and 2), up to approximately 120 days

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Number of Participants With Treatment-emergent Adverse Events (Arm A vs. Arm B)
secondaryOutcomes.description: Treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAE) are defined as those AEs with start or worsening date during the on-treatment period (from the first dose date of quizartinib/placebo to 30 days after the last dose date of quizartinib/placebo).
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Date of first dose up to 30 days after last dose, up to approximately 42 months

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Key Inclusion Criteria:

1. Must be competent and able to comprehend, sign, and date an Ethics Committee (EC)- or Institutional Review Board (IRB)-approved ICF before performance of any trial-specific procedures or tests.
2. ≥18 years or the minimum legal adult age (whichever is greater) and ≤70 years (at Screening).
3. Newly diagnosed, morphologically documented primary AML based on the World Health Organization (WHO) 2016 classification (at Screening)
4. Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status (at the time the participant signs their ICF) of 0-2.
5. Participant is a candidate for standard "7+3" induction chemotherapy regimen as specified in the protocol per investigator assessment

Key Exclusion Criteria:

1. Diagnosis of acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL), French-American-British classification M3 or WHO classification of APL with translocation, t(15;17)(q22;q12), or BCR-ABL positive leukemia (ie, chronic myelogenous leukemia in blast crisis); participants who undergo diagnostic workup for APL and treatment with all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA), but who are found not to have APL, are eligible (treatment with ATRA must be discontinued before starting induction chemotherapy).
2. Diagnosis of AML secondary to prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy.
3. Diagnosis of AML with known antecedent myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) or a myeloproliferative neoplasm (MPN) or MDS/MPNs including chronic myelomonocytic leukemia (CMML), atypical chronic myeloid leukemia (aCML), juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia (JMML) and others.
4. Participants with newly diagnosed AML with FLT3-ITD mutations (FLT3-ITD \[+\]) present at ≥5% VAF (or ≥0.05 SR) based on a validated FLT3 mutation assay.
5. Prior treatment for AML, except for the following allowances prior to Day 1 of chemotherapy:

   1. Leukapheresis;
   2. Treatment for hyperleukocytosis with hydroxyurea;
   3. Cranial radiotherapy for central nervous system (CNS) leukostasis;
   4. Prophylactic intrathecal chemotherapy
